metadata.source: CDC, NIMH, SAMHSA, American Psychological Association, National Alliance on Mental Illness
metadata.description: Risk factors and causes contributing to youth mental health issues
metadata.note: Evidence-based risk factors from clinical research and epidemiological studies

risk_factors.name: Genetic Predisposition
risk_factors.description: Mental health conditions often run in families. If parents or siblings have depression or anxiety, youth are at higher risk.
risk_factors.prevalence: 30-40% genetic component

risk_factors.name: Brain Chemistry Imbalances
risk_factors.description: Imbalances in neurotransmitters like serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine can contribute to mental health disorders.
risk_factors.prevalence: Affects 20-30% of youth with depression

risk_factors.name: Hormonal Changes During Adolescence
risk_factors.description: Puberty and teenage years involve major hormonal shifts that can trigger mood changes and increase mental health disorder risk.
risk_factors.prevalence: Peak onset age 13-18 years

risk_factors.name: Sleep Disruption
risk_factors.description: Insufficient or disrupted sleep significantly increases risk for depression and anxiety in adolescents.
risk_factors.prevalence: 60% of teens get insufficient sleep

risk_factors.name: Academic Stress and Pressure
risk_factors.description: High academic expectations, testing pressure, and competitive school environments contribute to anxiety and depression.
risk_factors.prevalence: 40% of students report high academic stress

risk_factors.name: Social Media and Cyberbullying
risk_factors.description: Excessive social media use, social comparison, and cyberbullying significantly impact youth mental health.
risk_factors.prevalence: 59% of teens experience cyberbullying

risk_factors.name: Peer Pressure and Social Isolation
risk_factors.description: Negative peer influence, social exclusion, and difficulty maintaining friendships increase mental health risks.
risk_factors.prevalence: 35% of youth experience social anxiety

risk_factors.name: Family Conflict and Instability
risk_factors.description: Parental conflict, divorce, abuse, or family dysfunction creates chronic stress affecting mental health.
risk_factors.prevalence: 40% of children experience parental conflict effects

risk_factors.name: Trauma and Adverse Experiences
risk_factors.description: Past or ongoing trauma, abuse, neglect, or significant losses increase depression, anxiety, and PTSD risk.
risk_factors.prevalence: 70% of youth experience at least one trauma

risk_factors.name: Discrimination and Marginalization
risk_factors.description: Experiencing racism, discrimination, or belonging to stigmatized groups increases mental health risks significantly.
risk_factors.prevalence: Disproportionate rates in marginalized communities

risk_factors.name: Economic Stress and Poverty
risk_factors.description: Financial instability, poverty, and economic uncertainty create chronic stress affecting mental health.
risk_factors.prevalence: 40% of poor youth have mental health conditions

risk_factors.name: Developmental Brain Changes
risk_factors.description: Adolescent brain development, particularly in emotion regulation and impulse control areas, increases vulnerability.
risk_factors.prevalence: Normal developmental process affecting all teens

risk_factors.name: Identity Formation Challenges
risk_factors.description: Struggles with sexual orientation, gender identity, or cultural identity can increase mental health vulnerability.
risk_factors.prevalence: LGBTQ+ youth have 3-4x higher mental health disorder rates

risk_factors.name: School Transitions and Major Changes
risk_factors.description: Moving, school changes, parental job loss, or other major life transitions disrupt stability and increase risk.
risk_factors.prevalence: Transitions affect most youth at some point

risk_factors.name: Substance Use and Experimentation
risk_factors.description: Alcohol or drug use, often as self-medication, worsens mental health and creates additional health risks.
risk_factors.prevalence: 25% of teens with mental illness use substances

risk_factors.name: Global Events and News Anxiety
risk_factors.description: Anxiety about climate, politics, pandemics, and global crises creates significant stress and uncertainty.
risk_factors.prevalence: 62% of teens worried about future

risk_factors.name: Perfectionism and High Self-Expectations
risk_factors.description: Unrealistic self-expectations and perfectionism lead to chronic stress, anxiety, and depression.
risk_factors.prevalence: 40% of high-achieving students are perfectionists

risk_factors.name: Lack of Physical Activity
risk_factors.description: Sedentary lifestyle increases depression and anxiety risk; exercise is protective.
risk_factors.prevalence: 75% of teens don't meet exercise guidelines

risk_factors.name: Chronic Medical Conditions
risk_factors.description: Youth with chronic illnesses (diabetes, asthma, etc.) have higher rates of depression and anxiety.
risk_factors.prevalence: 2-3x higher mental health disorder risk

risk_factors.name: Limited Access to Mental Health Services
risk_factors.description: Lack of insurance, providers, or stigma prevents youth from accessing needed mental health care.
risk_factors.prevalence: 75% of youth don't receive mental health treatment
